newsitem.title: CHINA: Hopewell says no word on Bangkok project.
newsitem.headline: Hopewell says no word on Bangkok project.

text.p: Hopewell Holdings Ltd said it had heard nothing on Thursday from the Thai government regarding the company's 30-year concession to build and operate a Bangkok multi-level rail and highway network.

The company said it was very surprised by the statement from a Thai official that the government could exercise its contractual right to scrap the concession awarded to Hopewell in 1990 as the firm had failed to meet its obligations.
"Hopewell Holdings is very surprised at this statement and has heard nothing from the Thai Government today," the company said in a statement.
"Hopewell had a very successful meeting with the Thai Government last Friday July 18. Hopewell Holdings remains very much committed to the project," it said.

Sathien Wongvichien, Deputy Permanent Secretary for Transport and Communications, said: "If (Hopewell) cannot come up with a firm financing package by the end of July, the communications ministry can scrap the contract... until now, it has failed to meet construction schedules in completing Phase One in time for the Bangkok Asian Games in late 1998."
Sathien said the government would probably find new investors to carry on the long-delayed project, with Hopewell scaling down its role from project operator to its future shareholder.

Hopewell said on Friday that it was unable to complete the project as planned because of adverse Thai economic conditions and the baht's fall, but said it wanted to complete the project and work with the government to overcome financing difficulties.
Hopewell chairman Gordon Wu said earlier this week that the weak baht had inflated costs by 15 percent.
Wu added that bankers were ready to fund the project but said he was not ready to take the money until he got a promise of a fare rise from the government.
